    SEO

    What is Search Intent?

    The underlying purpose behind a search query: whether the user wants information, navigation, comparison, or to make a purchase.

    KeywordSERPSEOGEOContent OptimizationAI CitationFeatured SnippetSearch VolumeZero-Click Search

    Search intent describes what a user actually wants when they type a query. There are four types: Informational ("what is GEO"), Navigational ("Halox login"), Commercial ("best SEO tools 2026"), and Transactional ("buy SEO software").

    Google's ranking system is built around intent matching. A perfectly keyword-optimized page won't rank if it serves the wrong intent. If the top 10 results for your keyword are all blog posts, Google considers it informational — publishing a product page there will fail regardless of your backlink profile.

    The 4 Types of Search Intent

    IntentSignal WordsExampleBest Content
    Informationalwhat, how, why, guide"what is GEO"Guide, glossary, tutorial
    Navigationalbrand name, login"Halox dashboard"Product page, login
    Commercialbest, review, vs, compare"Halox vs Ahrefs"Comparison, listicle
    Transactionalbuy, pricing, sign up"Halox pricing"Landing page, pricing

    Mixed intent exists too — "SEO tools" could be informational or commercial. Google shows mixed SERP features for these queries. Check the actual SERP to see how Google interprets each keyword before creating content.

    Intent-Based Content Strategy

    Informational — Comprehensive guides that fully answer the question. Clear definitions and FAQ sections increase AI citation potential. These pages build topical authority and attract backlinks.

    Commercial — Comparison pages with objective pros/cons, pricing, and clear recommendations. E-E-A-T signals (first-hand experience) are critical. AI models frequently cite comparison content for "best X" queries.

    Transactional — Clean landing pages with clear CTAs, pricing, and trust signals. Every extra step loses conversions.

    The SERP check rule: Before creating content, search the keyword and study what ranks. If Google shows videos, make video content. If AI Overviews dominate, structure content with quotable definitions and data for AI citation.

    Why It Matters

    “

    Intent alignment is one of the most important ranking factors in modern SEO. It also shapes AI citation patterns in GEO — when a user asks an AI "what is the best CRM?", the model interprets commercial intent and cites comparison content, not product pages. Creating content that matches intent helps you rank in Google and get cited by AI.

    How Halox Helps

    Halox displays intent data for every keyword in the Keyword Dashboard: Intent Tag: Each keyword is tagged with its intent type (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational) based on SERP and keyword analysis data: Intent-Based Filtering: Filter your keyword list by intent type to plan content across the funnel: SERP Context: See what SERP features Google shows for each keyword, which reveals how Google interprets its intent

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Search the keyword and look at the top 10 results. All how-to guides → informational. Product pages → transactional. Comparison posts → commercial. SERP features also help: PAA boxes suggest informational, shopping results suggest transactional. Keyword modifiers (what, how, buy, best) are additional signals.

    Yes. Google continuously re-evaluates intent based on user behavior. A keyword that was informational may shift to commercial as the topic matures. For example, "AI search" was purely informational a couple of years ago but now shows commercial results (tools, platforms). Check SERP changes for your target keywords regularly.

    Yes. AI models interpret user prompts by intent, just like Google. When someone asks "what is the best CRM?", the AI cites comparison content. When they ask "what is CRM?", it cites definitions. Matching content to the likely prompt intent increases the chance of being cited.

    Related Terms

    SEO

    Keyword

    A word or phrase that users type into search engines. Keywords are the foundation of SEO strategy, guiding content creation and optimization efforts.

    Learn more

    SEO

    SERP

    The page displayed by a search engine in response to a query. Modern SERPs include organic results, featured snippets, AI overviews, and other rich features.

    Learn more

    SEO

    SEO

    The practice of optimizing websites and content to rank higher in search engine results pages (SERPs), increasing organic visibility and traffic.

    Learn more

    GEO & AI Visibility

    GEO

    The practice of optimizing content to be cited and referenced by AI-powered search engines and language models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. The AI-era complement to traditional SEO.

    Learn more

    Content & Optimization

    Content Optimization

    The process of improving content to better satisfy search intent, improve search rankings, and increase the likelihood of being cited by AI models.

    Learn more

    GEO & AI Visibility

    AI Citation

    When an AI model references or recommends a specific brand, product, or source in its generated response. Citations are the currency of GEO — they determine whether your brand appears when users ask AI for recommendations.

Frequently Asked Questions
01
How do I determine search intent for a keyword?

Search the keyword and look at the top 10 results. All how-to guides → informational. Product pages → transactional. Comparison posts → commercial. SERP features also help: PAA boxes suggest informational, shopping results suggest transactional. Keyword modifiers (what, how, buy, best) are additional signals.

02
Can intent change over time?

Yes. Google continuously re-evaluates intent based on user behavior. A keyword that was informational may shift to commercial as the topic matures. For example, "AI search" was purely informational a couple of years ago but now shows commercial results (tools, platforms). Check SERP changes for your target keywords regularly.

03
Does search intent affect AI citations in GEO?

Yes. AI models interpret user prompts by intent, just like Google. When someone asks "what is the best CRM?", the AI cites comparison content. When they ask "what is CRM?", it cites definitions. Matching content to the likely prompt intent increases the chance of being cited.
